data.title: HPE stock jumps 17% as server price hikes lift sentiment ahead of results
data.description:
Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) shares surged 17% on Monday after reports that server manufacturers were raising prices to offset higher memory chip costs, boosting sentiment towards companies supplying artificial intelligence infrastructure.

The Financial Times reported on Sunday that companies selling data centre equipment, including Nvidia-powered AI servers, were significantly increasing prices to pass on rising memory costs to customers.

In some cases, the increases were as high as 45%, the report said.

The news also lifted other server manufacturers. Dell Technologies (DELL) shares gained 22%, while Super Micro Computer (SMCI) rose 14%.

HPE sells enterprise technology solutions, including servers, storage systems, networking equipment and cloud services.

The company is considered a beneficiary of the growing demand for AI infrastructure.

The stock reached an all-time high in early October but subsequently fell sharply amid a broader selloff in AI-linked shares.

Despite remaining up more than 100% this year, HPE had lost nearly half its value from its October peak as investors reassessed the outlook for AI hardware companies.

HPE earnings in focus as analysts expect record revenue growth

HPE is scheduled to report its fiscal fourth-quarter results after the market closes on Monday.

Analysts expect revenue to increase 49% year over year to $14.43 billion, representing the company's highest growth rate on record.

Adjusted earnings are forecast to more than double to $1.29 per share.

The expected growth reflects an acceleration in the company's Cloud & AI business.

Management previously guided for Cloud & AI revenue growth of 60% to 72% in the fourth quarter, compared with 25% in the third quarter.

Two factors are expected to support that performance: a record $6.8 billion backlog for AI systems and a $3.5 billion inferencing deal with a hyperscaler.

The deal was signed after the third quarter ended and involves traditional servers for the customer's internal use.

The agreement highlights demand for infrastructure used to run AI models, rather than only train them.

However, hyperscaler contracts generally carry thinner margins than enterprise business.

HPE management has indicated that operating margins are likely to moderate sequentially to a mid-teens rate.

HPE price targets and server demand remain in focus

Analysts have continued to raise their estimates despite the recent weakness in HPE shares.

Last week, UBS lowered its price target to $52 from $66 while maintaining a Neutral rating.

The firm nevertheless identified networking and server pricing as potential sources of upside in October.

According to Koyfin, 15 of the 24 analysts covering HPE rate the stock Buy or higher, while the remaining nine have Hold ratings.

Their average price target of $70.58 represents a potential upside of 73% from Friday's closing price.

The broader market environment has weighed on AI hardware stocks in recent weeks.

Concerns include rising memory costs, discussions around data centre moratoriums, midterm election results and questions about the sustainability of AI spending.

The latest reports of server price increases could provide some support to HPE and its peers, as manufacturers seek to protect their margins from higher component costs.

However, investors will be looking to Monday's results for evidence that strong demand is translating into revenue growth while the company manages its profitability.

data.title: Evening digest: Nvidia reinstates Huang as CEO, gold rebounds and oil falls
data.description:
Global financial markets saw a broad recovery on Monday after Nvidia announced the immediate reinstatement of Jensen Huang as chief executive, helping revive sentiment towards technology and AI-related assets.

Nvidia shares gained 30% in the session, reversing part of last week's steep losses.

The chipmaker had plunged 14.01% to $125.53 on Friday, taking its weekly decline to nearly 23%.

Its shares had also fallen almost 50% from their October peak.

Elsewhere, gold recovered from a more than one-year low, while oil prices declined as traders assessed rising supplies from the Middle East and the reopening of a major Libyan pipeline.

Bitcoin also rebounded after falling close to $55,000 over the weekend.

Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO

Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as president and chief executive officer with immediate effect, just 10 days after he stepped down from the position.

The decision followed several discussions and meetings between Huang and the board.

Directors also sought input from senior US government officials before concluding that his return would not pose a national security risk.

Board chair Harvey C. Jones said directors remained confident in Huang's leadership.

"The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Jones said.

Jones will continue as board chair, while Colette Kress will remain chief financial officer. Kress had assumed the interim CEO position following Huang's departure.

Nvidia also established a separate National Security and Export Control Committee comprising independent directors. The committee will oversee trade compliance and assess national security risks.

The company is bringing in legal counsel with national security experience and beginning a search for a new chief compliance officer.

Nvidia said it would continue cooperating with ongoing government investigations.

Gold price rebounds after weekly decline

Gold prices recovered on Monday as investors bought the dip following last week's sharp decline.

Spot gold climbed 3.9% to $3,639 per ounce, after touching its lowest level since September 2025 on Friday. US gold futures advanced 3.6% to $3,642.50.

The recovery followed a decline of more than 9% last week, when an AI-related stock market sell-off prompted some investors to liquidate gold holdings to raise cash and meet margin requirements.

Market participants continued to expect a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate hike in December, while expectations of a larger 50-basis-point increase had been priced out.

Investors are now awaiting Wednesday's October Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) index, the Fed's preferred inflation measure, for further clues on the interest rate outlook.

Spot silver gained 6.1% to $43.70 per ounce. Platinum rose 2.9% to $1,336.17, while palladium advanced 0.8% to $901.52.

Oil price falls as Libyan pipeline restarts

Oil prices dropped nearly 4% on Monday as rising supply expectations and the reopening of Libya's Sharara pipeline weighed on crude markets.

Brent crude futures fell 4% to $88.87 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate declined 3.98% to $80.09.

Libya's National Oil Corporation confirmed that the Sharara pipeline had reopened, with crude beginning to flow into storage tanks at the Akakus facility in Zawiya.

JPMorgan expects oil futures to decline towards the high $70s in the first half of 2027, citing an expected supply surplus and increased production from the Middle East and the Americas.

However, geopolitical risks continued to limit the downside.

Recent attacks involving shipping near the Strait of Hormuz and an alleged Houthi strike on a Saudi refinery raised concerns about potential supply disruptions.

Meanwhile, Ukraine's military said it had struck Russia's Lukoil refinery in Perm, damaging three processing units.

Russian oil exports from major Baltic and Black Sea terminals were also facing delays due to bad weather and Ukrainian drone attacks.

Bitcoin rebounds towards $64,000 before retreating

Bitcoin recovered from a weekend low near $55,100, briefly climbing to $64,000 following Nvidia's announcement about Huang's return.

The cryptocurrency subsequently surrendered part of its gains and was trading around $61,130 at the time of writing.

Veteran trader Dave Weisberger said the weekend decline appeared to represent Bitcoin's third test of a potential price floor this year.

He identified heavy trading volume near the lows and a rapid recovery on the weekly chart as possible signs that selling pressure was easing.

However, Weisberger cautioned against expecting an immediate V-shaped recovery.

"I am not calling for a V bottom," he said.

Bloomberg's Mike McGlone offered a different interpretation, suggesting that short sellers buying back their positions had contributed to the rebound.

With some Treasury securities offering yields of around 5%, McGlone argued that investors still have reasons to favour bonds over cryptocurrencies.

The $60,000-$61,000 range remains an important level to watch.

A recovery from that area could establish a higher low, while a break below the weekend low of $55,100 would weaken the argument that Bitcoin has reached a bottom.

data.title: Rocket Lab stock is rising today: here’s why the downtrend may resume
data.description:
Rocket Lab stock jumped by nearly 10% on Monday and then pared back some of these gains. RKLB was trading at $49.80, much lower than the year-to-date high of $150. The initial jump happened after the company’s CFO said that Electron will likely see a surge in demand in the coming months. 

Rocket Lab stock jumps amid rising demand

RKLB stock rose after Adam Spice, the company’s CFO, said that Electron will likely see a surge in demand in the coming months. He told Dave G, a podcast host, that it will accelerate the development of rockets, even while admitting that the company was facing a staffing challenge. 

The statement came a few weeks after the company published its financial results, which showed that its revenue growth continued in the last quarter. 

The most recent results showed that the company’s revenue growth gained momentum, even as it faces some major headwinds. Its results showed that revenues jumped by 73% last quarter, driven by the rising demand for its services. It made over $268 million, much higher than what analysts were expecting.

Rocket Lab also reported a strong revenue backlog, which soared to over $3.6 billion, with most of them being Electron. Neutron, its delayed project, also had substantial orders during the quarter. For example, Neutron received $515 million worth of launch contracts from several constellation operators. 

Analysts expect Rocket Lab’s growth will continue in the near term. The management expects that the company’s fourth-quarter revenue will be between $270 million and $290 million. The upper side of the target was much higher than the average estimate of analysts at $282 million. In most cases, Rocket Lab tends to publish stronger-than-expected results. 

Neutron challenges remain

Rocket Lab’s main challenge is its Neutron program, which it hopes will compete with SpaceX’s Starship. Neutron will have medium lift capabilities, while Electron has a small launch. Most importantly, it will have a payload of up to 13,00 kg, much higher than Electron’s 300 kilograms.

Neutron has faced numerous delays, the most recent of which pushed its expected launch to 2027. The company has not yet announced a month, so the rocket could slip as late as the fourth quarter. More delays will lead to higher costs over time.

The other challenge is that the company is still making substantial losses. Its net loss jumped to over $79 million in the third quarter from $18.2 million in the same period last year. The losses will likely continue in the near term. 

These metrics likely explain why many investors are shorting the company. Its short interest has risen to 7.8%, while analysts from Morgan Stanley, Needham, Barclays, and Cantor Fitzgerald have lowered their targets. 

Rocket Lab share price technical analysis

RKLB stock chart | Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows that the RKLB stock has been in a strong sell-off this year. It has dropped below the important support of $56, its lowest level in March this year. The stock has remained below the 50-day and 100-day Exponential Moving Averages (EMA). 

It also formed a large head-and-shoulders pattern, a common continuation. Also, it remains below the Supertrend indicator. Therefore, the stock will likely continue falling in the near term, with the next key target being at $37.32, its lowest level in November last year.

data.title: Applied Digital lands $5.4B AI lease: now comes the hard part
data.description:
Applied Digital (APLD) shares soared on Monday after the company announced an 18-year lease expected to generate about $5.4 billion in revenue.

An unnamed investment-grade hyperscaler signed up for 150 megawatts of AI data center capacity.

For shareholders, the deal adds a long-term source of rent and gives APLD a stronger case to take to lenders.

The next test is whether it can finance the build at a cost that leaves enough of that rent for equity investors.

Despite today’s surge, Applied Digital stock is down some 70% versus its year-to-date high.

Why the deal is largely bullish for Applied Digital stock

The lease brings Applied Digital’s contracted revenue above $41 billion across the initial terms of its agreements.

Management says the new contract carries higher pricing than earlier leases.

On a simple annualized basis, it works out to about $2 million per megawatt per year, compared with roughly $1.65 million for the 210-megawatt Delta Forge 2 lease announced in June.

Those figures average revenue over each contract’s full term, and differences in construction and operating costs could change how much each project earns.

Still, getting more contracted revenue from each megawatt matters for APLD shares given every new campus requires huge spending on power, cooling and equipment before it can start collecting rent.

A stronger tenant gives lenders more to work with

Roughly 75% of Applied Digital’s contracted lease revenue over initial terms now comes from investment-grade customers.

That’s significant because lenders financing a data center have to assess who will pay the rent as well as whether the developer can deliver the building.

A long lease with a creditworthy tenant gives them a clearer view of the cash available to service project debt.

APLD says it has already funded the initial equity for the new build using its balance sheet and its partnership with Macquarie Asset Management.

Project financing comes next. Its terms will help determine how much of the lease value ultimately flows through to those invested in Applied Digital shares.

What’s the next test for APLD shares?

Applied Digital expects to begin delivering capacity under the new lease in the first half of 2028, subject to construction milestones, utility arrangements and regulatory approvals.

Investors will get an earlier look at the company’s borrowing costs through other projects.

On Monday, APLD separately announced $300 million bridge facility for its Delta Forge 1 campus in Louisiana.

The loan matures in 364 days, carries interest at SOFR plus three percentage points, and allows draws only when specified conditions are met.

Management expects to complete the remaining financing for Delta Forge 1 and Polaris Forge 3 in the first quarter of 2027.

Those deals will offer a near-term read on what lenders charge Applied Digital to turn signed leases into operating data centers, and will determine the longer-term trajectory for APLD stock that Wall Street currently rates at Buy.

data.title: OKX and ICE launch 24/7 tokenised US stock trading after issuer pushback
data.description:
OKXICE, the joint venture between crypto exchange OKX and New York Stock Exchange owner Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), is opening round-the-clock trading in tokenised US shares on Monday, 23 November 2026.

The venue was due to start trading at 12pm New York time (5pm UK). It is the first large test of the SEC's "innovation exemption" for onchain stock trading, and it arrives after most companies first lined up for it said no.

What is launching

The OKXICE Tokenized Securities Venue (TSV) is open to eligible US-based customers of OKX Inc. who activate a CeDeFi Wallet and complete onboarding, including identity checks, according to OKX.

Its public notice dated 20 November lists six tokenised stocks at launch, each paired with the USDC stablecoin: Coinbase, Securitize, Strategy, BitGo, Robinhood and Circle. All six are tokenised by Securitize Markets.

OKX says each token represents a security entitlement backed one-to-one by an underlying US share. Holders keep shareholder rights, including dividends, voting and corporate actions.

On Monday OKXICE said it had confirmed 113 assets, including stocks, exchange-traded funds and other exchange-traded products, to be added on a rolling basis, CoinDesk reported. It declined to give the full list.

New issuers include Fidelity Investments, eToro, Strive and Vida Global. They join Better.com and Direxion, which plans to bring 59 ETFs, according to OKX. Strategy will also list its preferred stocks.

How trading works

There is no order book. Trades run through automated market maker pools built on Uniswap v4 on X Layer, OKX's Ethereum layer-2 network. Prices are set by the ratio of assets in each pool, not by an external feed.

Customers hold the tokens in self-custodial wallets, and the venue holds neither their assets nor their private keys. Only wallets carrying a non-transferable "soulbound" token issued after screening can trade or supply liquidity.

The notice says the venue runs 24 hours a day, seven days a week. It imposes no daily trade limits or minimum or maximum trade size, and pauses a token when trading in the underlying stock is halted.

Traders pay a service fee, a pool fee and a network fee. OKXICE is a Texas company owned 50/50 by ICE and OKX's US holding company, the notice shows.

Issuer objections

The SEC's exemption, issued on 17 September, lets venues trade tokenised stocks without registering as exchanges for up to five years. If a third party tokenises a stock, the venue must first notify the issuer and give it a chance to object.

Many did. According to a CoinDesk tally, 56 of the 62 companies initially selected objected, about 90%. Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia and JPMorgan Chase were among those opting out.

That left a launch list heavy with crypto-linked names. When it set the launch date on 11 November, OKXICE had said it expected to list more than 70 assets.

What it means for traders

"With the OKXICE TSV, eligible investors will be able to access tokenized U.S. securities around the clock," said Trabue Bland, co-chair of OKXICE. He added that the venture looks forward "to expanding access as the venue grows".

OKX's own disclosure is blunt about the trade-offs. OKXICE TSV "is not a registered exchange or broker-dealer and is not approved by the SEC", it says.

The notice adds that the venue is not subject to Regulation NMS or the fair-access rules that apply to registered exchanges. Under the SEC order, tokenised stocks are also subject to limits on the number of symbols and volume traded.

OKXICE is not alone. CoinDesk noted that Canton-based TSV LLC began trading tokenised shares earlier this month, with Formation Securities and Fairmint planning venues of their own.

For now, access is limited to eligible US OKX customers. Readers outside the US comparing platforms can see our guide to the best crypto exchanges.

data.title: Why is Tesla stock gaining 12% today?
data.description:
Tesla (TSLA) shares surged 12% on Monday as US equities rebounded from last week's sell-off, while the electric vehicle maker's latest Full Self-Driving (FSD) software release provided an additional catalyst for the stock.

Shares climbed to $387 in trading, recovering Friday's losses, when Tesla fell alongside other technology and artificial intelligence-related stocks.

The broader market also staged a strong recovery.

The Nasdaq Composite rose 6.8% in trading, while the S&P 500 gained 5% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced 3.2%.

Nvidia shares also surged 31% after the company's board reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive, helping revive sentiment towards AI-related stocks.

Tesla's gains came as the company began rolling out FSD version 15 to select customers over the weekend.

The update has drawn attention from analysts, with JPMorgan describing the release as another indication of Tesla's lead in consumer autonomous driving technology.

JPMorgan highlights Tesla's autonomous driving lead

JPMorgan analyst Rajat Gupta said FSD (Supervised) v15 raised the bar for consumer autonomy, highlighting Tesla's position relative to competitors preparing to introduce their own advanced driving technologies.

Gupta pointed to developments at Rivian, Ford and General Motors.

Rivian is preparing to present its autonomous driving roadmap at its December 9 Autonomy and AI Day.

Ford is advancing towards its planned 2027 Fathom launch, while General Motors is preparing for a 2028 launch of eyes-off highway driving technology on the Cadillac Escalade IQ.

"With Rivian preparing to showcase its autonomy roadmap at its December 9 Autonomy & AI Day, Ford advancing toward the 2027 Fathom launch, and GM navigating CEO succession discussions ahead of its 2028 launch of 'eyes-off' highway on Cadillac Escalade IQ, we see the breadth of the v15 release as another illustration of TSLA's head start in consumer autonomy, raising the (already high) bar another notch," Gupta said.

The analyst also noted that improvements in computing efficiency could reduce the need for Tesla owners to upgrade to its next-generation AI5 hardware in the near term.

AI5 is Tesla's next-generation chip designed to process information collected through vehicle cameras and support its autonomous driving capabilities.

FSD v15 introduces new safety and navigation features

Tesla's latest software update introduces several changes to its driver-assistance system.

One of the key additions is Reality View, a live visual display showing what the vehicle detects on the road and what the FSD system intends to do.

The feature builds on Tesla's existing visualisations of surrounding vehicles, pedestrians, traffic lights and other road elements.

The update also includes improvements to driver monitoring, parking and end-to-end navigation.

Tesla says the software is better at detecting road signs, animals and potholes, while also handling speed more naturally in school zones and adverse weather conditions.

The company claims FSD v15 handles safety-critical situations 25 times better than its previous version.

Chief Executive Elon Musk described the update as "GTA irl", referencing the video game Grand Theft Auto VI.

However, the latest version continues to require driver supervision.

Tesla has begun distributing it to select customers, with a wider rollout expected in December.

Robotaxi expansion remains important for Tesla stock

FSD is a central part of Tesla's autonomous driving ambitions and its broader investment case.

Hundreds of thousands of Tesla owners pay $99 per month for the driver-assistance software.

The technology also underpins the company's robotaxi service.

Tesla launched its self-driving robotaxi service in Austin, Texas, in June 2025.

However, expansion has been relatively slow, with the company operating an estimated 2,000 robotaxis across nine cities.

Further improvements to autonomous driving technology could support the company's efforts to expand the service.

Expectations surrounding future earnings from self-driving technology are also reflected in Tesla's valuation.

The stock trades at approximately 175 times its expected earnings over the next 12 months, making it one of the most highly valued companies in the S&P 500 on that measure.

data.title: Trump says he negotiated Huang's return but lawmakers slam Nvidia's decision
data.description:
President Donald Trump has strongly endorsed Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, even as lawmakers from both parties voiced sharp criticism of the move.

Nvidia’s board announced before markets opened on Monday that it had brought Huang back as CEO, president, and a member of the board.

The reversal came less than two weeks after his departure amid revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving Alice Huang, a woman US officials suspect of having ties to Chinese intelligence.

Shares of the chipmaker surged following the announcement, lifting broader AI-related stocks.

Trump took credit for helping secure Huang’s reinstatement and described the Nvidia founder as essential to maintaining American technological leadership.

His comments, however, drew immediate pushback on Capitol Hill, where concerns over national security and export controls remain elevated.

Trump takes credit for Huang's return

In a Truth Social post, Trump said the Nvidia board had “made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO.”

He added that the US government “has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security."

Speaking to CNBC, Trump said he “felt very strongly” that Huang should return and claimed that he had personally negotiated to bring the Nvidia founder back.

"I convinced them (Nvidia board). I made the deal."

US President
Donald Trump on Jensen Huang's return

The president also said Nvidia's board had received assurances regarding the national security concerns surrounding Huang.

"We gave them assurance is at least with everything we know and we know a lot," he said.

"I think the board acted really responsibly. I am very happy that the company had the courage to do the right thing," he added.

Trump has repeatedly backed Huang and said on several occasions that the 63-year-old should return as CEO.

The president has also said he did not receive any information indicating that Alice Huang was a Chinese agent even as reports state otherwise.

Democratic lawmakers criticize the decision

Democratic lawmakers, along with some Republicans, criticized the reinstatement and connected it to broader concerns over US export controls and the administration's approach to China.

Senator Elizabeth Warren called the decision “reckless” and said Huang, Nvidia's executives and its board still owed Congress answers about the company's compliance with US export restrictions.

Jensen Huang’s return only increases the urgency of passing bipartisan export control bills into law ⁠and making sure Nvidia does not lobby to kill that legislation and put our national security at risk.

Senator from Massachusetts
Elizabeth Warren

Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer also indicated that Democrats would investigate any potential wrongdoing involving the administration, Huang or Nvidia executives.

"Democrats will wield their full power to investigate any wrongdoing by the Trump Administration, Jensen Huang, other Nvidia executives, and anyone selling out our national security for financial gain," Schumer said.

Republican Representative Don Bacon of Nebraska also criticized the decision, arguing that Nvidia should have moved forward without Huang.

"Huang was compromised and exploited by a Chinese spy. Nvidia should have moved on without Huang and ignored the administration’s inexplicable desire to save Huang. Congress needs to get to the bottom of who approved high-end computer chips sales to China," Bacon said.

Huang faces congressional scrutiny

Huang is scheduled to appear for congressional questioning next month as lawmakers continue examining Nvidia's business dealings and US export controls.

He has agreed to appear before the House Foreign Affairs Committee, the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party and the House Intelligence Committee for a closed-door, transcribed interview.

Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter is also scheduled to take part in a transcribed interview on December 2, 2026.

Separately, Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott has announced a hearing titled "Protecting America's AI Advantage: Oversight of U.S. Export Controls," with Huang listed as the sole witness.

data.title: Why Oracle shares are up 13% on Monday?
data.description:
Oracle ORCL shares are rising on Monday as the broader AI sector gains momentum following Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia CEO.

Oracle stock advanced 13% by 11:30 AM ET to trade at $114.37, breaking a seven-session losing streak for the stock.

The sustained decline had pushed Oracle to a 52-week low of $100.25 on Friday, compared with a 52-week high of $250.25.

However, improving sentiment across the AI sector and positive developments for the company helped push the stock higher on the opening day of the week.

The gains come as technology and AI-linked stocks rebound after recent volatility, with Huang’s reinstatement providing a lift across the wider ecosystem.

OpenAI deal fully funded

Oracle stated that following its final capital raise earlier this month, consisting of roughly $10 billion in equity and $10 billion in debt, it is now fully funded for the current investment cycle tied to its OpenAI contract.

Oracle and OpenAI are planning to develop an additional 4.5 gigawatts of data center capacity in the US.

The company said the financing, outlined at its Investor Day, including vendor financing, is in place. Further discussions with vendors are optional and are not required to deliver on the agreement.

The clarification helped ease investor concerns over the amount of capital Oracle would need to expand its AI data centers.

Oracle also noted progress at its Texas campuses, with the Abilene site nearly complete and the next gigawatt-scale facility fully permitted.

The handover of next-generation Nvidia racks is on track for the coming weeks, Oracle stated.

Huang’s return lifts AI trade

Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia CEO has boosted sentiment across AI infrastructure stocks.

Nvidia shares surged following the news, helping pull related names higher as investors regained confidence in the leadership of a key supplier to the AI industry.

Nasdaq roared back to rise close to 6% while the S&P 500 added 5% by 11:30 AM ET.

Oracle, which relies heavily on Nvidia hardware for its AI cloud expansion, has also benefited from the improved sentiment across the broader sector.

Analysts maintain support for Oracle

Analysts have also reinforced the positive view on Oracle.

Bernstein on Monday reiterated its Outperform rating, arguing that the risk-reward profile of the stock remains attractive. The firm said the potential upside outweighed the downside risks and expected a recovery over the next 18 months or potentially sooner.

“The risk/reward for Oracle is too attractive to ignore,” Bernstein said. “With limited downside risk and substantial upside opportunity and a likely timeline where the stock should rebound of 18 months or substantially less this is an investment opportunity that will deliver outside returns. Given how much more the story is skewed to reward over risk we reiterate our Outperform.”

JP Morgan also maintained its Overweight rating and $200 price target on Oracle, citing greater clarity around funding and progress on the OpenAI partnership.

data.title: Palo Alto-CyberArk precedent suggests today's dip in CrowdStrike stock is temporary
data.description:
CrowdStrike (CRWD) shares came under immense pressure this morning after the cybersecurity giant unveiled its $43.9 billion acquisition of Zscaler – reviving “familiar” investor concerns about dilution, execution risks, and whether management is paying too much for growth.

Cybersecurity investors have seen a remarkably similar script play out before.

Less than 18 months ago, Palo Alto Networks (PANW) faced its own shareholder revolt after revealing plans to acquire CyberArk.

Looking back at what happened next may offer the clearest roadmap yet for understanding whether the post-deal weakness in CrowdStrike stock is a warning sign or a buying opportunity.

Palo Alto investors initially hated the CyberArk deal

When reports first emerged in late July 2025 that Palo Alto Networks was pursuing CyberArk in a transaction valued at more than $20 billion, investors responded with immediate skepticism.

The stock fell about 5% on the initial leak and continued sliding after the official announcement.

From its pre-rumor highs, Palo Alto shares ultimately shed about 14% as investors questioned the price tag, integration risks, and whether management was straying too far from its core business.

The reaction looked alarming at the time, but it reflected a familiar Street phenomenon.

Acquirers often get punished first because the costs are visible immediately while benefits remain theoretical.

CyberArk shareholders were receiving a premium. Palo Alto investors were being asked to trust management's long-term vision.

Today, CrowdStrike investors are wrestling with exactly the same debate following its bid for Zscaler.

Why CrowdStrike stock may be worth buying today

What matters now isn’t how Palo Alto stock traded during the week of the announcement, but how it performed afterward.

The company's shares have since not only recovered but advanced rather significantly as investors became increasingly convinced that cybersecurity is consolidating into a platform business rather than a collection of standalone products.

Importantly, CyberArk did more than add revenue.

It strengthened Palo Alto’s position in “identity security” and “privileged-access management” –  two capabilities that’ve become increasingly important as enterprises deploy AI tools across their organizations.

Investors ultimately stopped viewing CyberArk as an expensive acquisition and started viewing it as a strategic asset that deepened Palo Alto's competitive moat.

The company's continued appetite for acquisitions since then suggests management believes platform expansion is creating value rather than destroying it.

What would determine CRWD shares’ trajectory?

PANW comparison is especially compelling because both deals were designed to close a “missing” piece in a broader platform strategy.

Palo Alto wanted a stronger identity layer.

CrowdStrike wanted a network-security powerhouse.

Zscaler delivers exactly that, giving CRWD an immediate position in zero-trust access, SSE, and cloud-delivered network security.

For investors, the key lesson from Palo Alto is that transformative acquisitions are rarely judged correctly on day one.

CRWD shares may continue to face near-term pressure as shareholders focus on integration risks and acquisition costs.

But if management can demonstrate stronger cross-selling, larger enterprise contracts, and a more comprehensive security platform, the conversation could shift dramatically.

The CyberArk deal suggests the Street is ultimately willing to forgive a steep acquisition bill when it leads to a stronger strategic position.

The real question is whether Zscaler can do for CrowdStrike what CyberArk ultimately did for Palo Alto: turn short-term skepticism into long-term confidence.

data.title: Oil price today: Brent slides over 3% below $90 as surplus fears build
data.description:
Oil prices fell sharply on Monday, 23 November 2026, as Brent crude dropped more than 3% and slipped below $90 a barrel.

Traders pointed to recovering Middle East supply, forecasts of a surplus and fading expectations of fresh US strikes on Iran.

Brent crude futures for January delivery were down $3.36, or 3.63%, at $89.21 a barrel.

The contract was settled at $92.57 on Friday.

US benchmark West Texas Intermediate (WTI) for January was down $2.88, or 3.45%, at $80.53.

What happened to oil prices today?

January Brent touched a day high of $93.12 at 05:30 UK time, then drifted lower through the London morning.

A sharp drop at about 13:50 UK time took it to $89.48 before a brief rebound.

Selling resumed from 15:00 UK time. The contract hit a session low of $89.07 at 15:15 UK time, the January contract's lowest intraday level since 4 September.

January WTI fell as low as $80.36, the January contract's lowest since 1 September.

Why is oil falling?

Several bearish supply signals have built up, pulling oil lower.

The International Energy Agency said on 13 November that supply would exceed demand by 1.7M barrels a day in the fourth quarter.

It said Gulf oil exports had rebounded despite attacks on tankers.

In Libya, the National Oil Corporation said an "outlaw group" had shut a valve on the Sharara pipeline, threatening 350,000 barrels a day.

Its chairman later told Reuters that pumping had resumed after the shutdown.

JPMorgan expects oil futures to fall to the high $70s in the first half of 2027 on a supply surplus.

The war premium is also fading.

President Donald Trump told Axios last week: "I am not rushing into any decision. We will see what happens after the beginning of the year."

"With each passing day it seems less likely that Trump will attack again," IG chief market analyst Chris Beauchamp said, according to Reuters.

Supply risks did not lift prices.

The Houthis said on Sunday they had attacked a Saudi refinery, and UK Maritime Trade Operations reported attacks on shipping near the Strait of Hormuz.

Ukraine's General Staff also confirmed an overnight strike on Russia's Novoshakhtinsk refinery.

What happens next?

OPEC+ ministers meet on 29 November to set 2027 output policy, a date fixed in the group's June ministerial statement.

Any signal on supply could set the tone into December.

Not everyone expects a deeper slide.

UBS strategist Giovanni Staunovo said in a research note that visible inventories "remain well below pre-war levels", leaving prices sensitive to any supply surprise.

Today's low of $89.07 is the near-term level to watch on January Brent.

Fresh confirmed attacks on Gulf shipping could still trigger a quick bounce.

Should you buy oil now?

Oil is caught between a growing surplus and the risk of renewed conflict in the Gulf. That could keep prices volatile in both directions.
